content.title: How do the covenants connect the whole Bible?
content.summary: Follow God’s promises to their fulfillment in Christ without flattening the differences between the covenants.

answer.text: All the Baptist ways of reading the covenants share the main lines: God binds himself by promise; everyone saved in any age is saved by grace through faith in the promised Christ; and the new covenant, made in his blood, fulfils what the earlier covenants anticipated. Baptists hold four main frameworks for how the covenants fit together, set out below, and the site’s confession, the Baptist Faith and Message 2000, does not choose among them. Covenant theology in its Westminster (Presbyterian) form describes a covenant of works with Adam and a covenant of grace after the fall. The Old and New Testaments reveal the same saving Mediator through different administrations; the new covenant brings the fulfillment accomplished by his blood. The Baptist confession of 1689 agrees that everyone saved in any age is saved by the covenant of grace, but leaves out Westminster’s paragraphs on one covenant under two administrations: it says the covenant of grace was revealed by promise, step by step, and fully made known in the New Testament.

reasoning.text: Paul places Adam and Christ alongside one another as representative heads: condemnation comes through the first man’s disobedience, righteousness and life through the obedience of Christ.
The promise to Abraham is directed to Christ and received through faith. The later law does not cancel the promise; it serves within the history leading to Christ.
Hebrews announces the superiority of the new covenant and Christ’s once-for-all sacrifice. Continuity of salvation does not mean that every earlier ordinance continues unchanged.

conclusion.text: Read each passage in its historical covenant setting and in relation to Christ. The unity is God’s saving purpose; the movement is from promise and anticipation to fulfillment.

sections.text: Covenant of works names the confessional synthesis of Adam’s obligation and representative role; Genesis does not use that precise phrase in its creation narrative. Covenant of grace names salvation offered through Christ to fallen sinners. These categories should be argued from the texts rather than assumed because a system uses them.
sections.title: Distinguish the biblical words and the theological summary

sections.text: 1689 covenant theology, held by many Calvinist Baptists since Nehemiah Coxe and the Second London Confession, sees one covenant of grace promised from Genesis 3 onward and formally made in the new covenant, so its sign belongs only to those who profess faith. Progressive covenantalism stresses that each covenant moves the story forward until all are fulfilled in Christ, and that the new covenant is new in kind: all its members know the Lord. New covenant theology, close to it, holds that the law of Moses as a whole ended with Christ and that the law of Christ now governs believers. Dispensationalism, in its classic and progressive forms, distinguishes God’s purposes for Israel and for the church and expects a future fulfilment of his promises to Israel. Westminster covenant theology, the Presbyterian form, sees the covenant of grace given to believers and their children in both Testaments, which is why Presbyterians baptize infants; Baptists do not hold that form. Each view claims to follow the Bible’s own storyline, so compare them passage by passage.
sections.title: Four ways Baptists read the covenants

sections.text: The law exposes sin and guides the redeemed life. It does not give fallen sinners a separate route to justification by personal achievement. Westminster and the Baptist confession of 1689 distinguish moral, ceremonial and judicial law; those distinctions require attention to the passage and its fulfillment, not simply attaching the label Old Testament.
sections.title: What happens to the law?

content.objection: Does covenant theology force every passage into a predetermined system?

reply.text: It can be misused that way. A sound account must let the biblical passages correct its categories, preserve the historical differences and explain the new covenant’s superiority. Compare the whole argument of Hebrews and Galatians, rather than selecting isolated proof texts. A confession is useful precisely when its reasoning can be examined.

limit.text: This guide describes covenant theology in its Westminster and 1689 forms most fully because their confessions state it most precisely; that does not make either form the site’s position. The difference between them matters most for baptism: Westminster baptizes the infants of believers as members of the covenant (28.4), while the Baptist confession baptizes only those who profess repentance and faith (29.2), as does the site’s own confession, the Baptist Faith and Message 2000 (article VII). Use the library’s tradition and edition notes when comparing authors, and distinguish an agreed doctrine of grace from a disputed covenant inference.
